lines.text: Dolphins sleep with half their brain.
And wait till you see what their eyes do.
One half of the brain falls asleep. The other half stays awake.
Dolphins choose every breath, so the awake half swims up for air.
The eye linked to the sleeping half closes. The other eye stays open, on watch.
About two hours later, the halves swap.
lines.caption: About 2 hours later, the halves swap.

lines.text: In one study, dolphins stayed alert like this for fifteen days straight.
